title: Pinback escape hatch notes and shielding cheatsheet
content:
Context:
Quick personal scratchpad for fast pinbacks and service shielding during canary ramps. Purpose is not a formal runbook but a minimal, actionable checklist I can follow when I’m the on-call or coordinating a small team during a slow-roll. Keep this next to the monitor during quiet windows.

Top-level goal:
- Reduce blast radius quickly, preserve client experience, and buy time for investigation.

Key concepts (short):
- Pinback: force routing of traffic back to previous pinned model/image/version or to a safe replica pool.
- Shielding: divert new sessions / risky cohorts to a static fallback (lightweight model or cached answers) while preserving subset of traffic to the canary for diagnostics.
- Pause button: temporary stop acceptance on the updated route (0% new starts).

Quick decision tree (3 questions):
1) Is user-facing correctness clearly degraded? -> Pinback and notify clients.
2) Is latency or error rate the issue but not correctness? -> Shield cohorts, reduce concurrency, preserve small p99 sampling.
3) Is telemetry noisy/unreliable? -> Stabilize sampling and keep canary at a tiny fraction (0.5%-2%) while triaging.

Immediate actions (first 10 minutes):
- Grab pager details + timeline from Alerts dashboard. Link: /console/alerts/recent
- Announce in #oncall (template): "Activating pinback shield on route X; reducing canary -> safe; need owner@ 15 min".
- Execute pinback: POST to internal routing API or use infra cli:
  - infra route set-weights --route /generate --weights previous:100,new:0 --reason "pinback at <time>"
  - or curl: curl -X POST $ROUTER/api/v1/weights -d '{"route":"/generate","weights":{"stable":"100","canary":"0"}}'
- Confirm by watching request logs and 200/500 rate for 2 minutes.

Shielding pattern (if we need quiet investigation):
- Lower new session acceptance on canary: set-session-prob 0.01
- Enable cache-only fallback for low-confidence responses: feature-flag:response_shield=true
- Route signed enterprise clients to dedicated stable pool (if available).

Metrics to watch (thresholds I use):
- Errors: 5xx > 0.5% sustained for 3m -> escalate.
- Latency: p95 increase > 250ms over baseline -> consider shielding.
- Quality regressions: automated eval A/B NLL delta > 0.04 -> immediate pinback.
- Cost/per-token spike: +30% sudden -> check batching/quantization fallback.

Post-pin investigation checklist:
- Collect 1k sample requests from canary window (ids + prompts) -> put in /tmp/canary-samples-<ts>.json
- Run local reproduction with the same model binary + seed.
- Search for recent infra changes: PRs merged last 24h with label deployment: check github.com/redwood-inference/* (PRs referenced above).
- Check model artifacts and quantization metadata hashes.

Communication template (short):
Subject: "Pinback executed on /generate — moving canary -> stable; investigating"
Body: short summary, what we saw, action taken, owners, ETA for updates. Post to #release-ops and to affected client channel if enterprise.

Short commands and locations:
- Alerts: https://console.redwood/alerts
- Routing API: https://router.internal/api/v1/weights
- Canary samples: s3://redwood-canary-dumps/<date>/
- Debug shell: ssh infra-worker-<id>

Open questions / TODO (for followups):
- Do we want an automated graceful shrink to 1% before 0% for all routes? (Pros: catches flaky telemetry; cons: slower mitigation)
- Formalize shielding flag exposure to customers (currently infra-only).
- Add a cheap canary-responder that returns canned replies for enterprise clients during shielding.

Notes to self / heuristics I learned:
- Don’t yank to 0% if only 1 outlier client shows errors; try cohort isolation first.
- Always preserve sampling trace for at least 30 minutes after pinback for root cause.
- During high-traffic windows, prefer shielding over full pinback to prevent global regressions.

Postmortem stub (fill after incident):
- Timeline, root cause hypothesis, corrective actions, monitoring gaps, playbook changes.

Short checklist to commit to infra/ops later:
- Add an infra cli alias: rpb (route-pinback) that requires reason and owner.
- Add an automated traffic-scan that flags suspicious pattern deviations before deployment.
- Run table-top drill for pinback once per quarter.

End of scratchpad. Keep updated with links to Confluence and PRs. If I’m not available, Ethan should own the first 30 minutes.
